artists.biography: "Public Service Broadcasting"  are a London-based pseudonymous musical group consisting of J. Willgoose, Esq. on guitar, banjo, other stringed instruments, samplings and electronic musical instruments, Wrigglesworth on drums, piano and electronic musical instruments, and J F Abraham on flugelhorn, bass guitar, drums and assorted other instruments including a vibraslap. The band have toured internationally and in 2015 they were announced as nominees in the Vanguard breakthrough category of the fourth annual Progressive Music Awards, staged by Prog magazine, which they won.

perplexity.description:
Live At Brixton" is a live album by Public Service Broadcasting, released in 2016 on the Test Card Recordings label. The album captures the band's dynamic live performance at Brixton Academy, showcasing their distinctive blend of electronic music infused with historical and documentary samples. This release features live renditions of tracks primarily from their earlier studio albums, emphasizing their cinematic and instrumental approach that combines vintage audio clips with modern electronic production.

Musically, the album highlights Public Service Broadcasting's unique style, which merges electronic beats, brass instrumentation, and archival soundbites to create immersive soundscapes that evoke themes of history, technology, and exploration. As a live album, it serves as a significant entry in their discography by translating their studio concept albums into an engaging concert experience, reflecting their reputation for visually and sonically compelling shows.

Critically, "Live At Brixton" was well received for its energetic and precise live execution, though it peaked modestly at number 97 on the UK charts. It stands as an important document of the band's live capabilities and their ability to maintain the narrative and emotional impact of their studio work in a concert setting.
